Subject: RL training burst reservation / temporary autoscale exception

Hi team,

Orbit AI is ready to run a 48–72 hour RL training burst next week as part of their pilot (they've validated model correctness on smaller infra). They need a predictable slice of Dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbors and a temporary autoscale policy exception so their long-running gradient steps don't get evicted mid-episode.

Ask: can we carve a short-lived reservation (48 hours preferred, up to 72 if ops ok) on a single GPU pool and grant an autoscale exception that keeps the slice pinned at their reserved min until completion?

Why: the training runs are stateful and hold large KV caches; preemption mid-episode causes noisy corruption that loses days of progress. Orbit is willing to schedule the run during off-peak window and sign the usage MPA.

Attached: rl-training-burst-outline.pdf (high-level schedule), rl-sim-profile.csv (expected memory/throughput).

Next steps I propose:
- Infra: feasibility and constraints (GPU types, isolation level)
- Ops: runbook for emergency rollback and eviction policy during carve-out
- Sales/CS: confirm SOW / mutual action plan with Orbit so finance can approve

Bethany — fyi, please confirm the earliest window you can commit to next week.

Thanks,
Laura

Laura — thanks for the context. Quick questions before I scope the carve-out: 

1) GPU type preference? (A100-80GB / H100-80GB / other). We need to reserve homogeneous nodes to avoid scheduling issues.
2) Expected peak VRAM and sustained runtime per job (hours). The rl-sim-profile has some numbers but please call out the worst-case.
3) Does the workload rely on model kv-cache persistence across checkpoints, or can KV be reconstructed from checkpointed states?
4) Do you want us to allocate a strict reservation (isolated slice) or a soft reservation with priority lane + eviction guard?

Operational constraints we will require for an exception:
- Clear runbook with rollback trigger (e.g., >85% system load, infra incident)
- Auto-rollback to default autoscale policy after X hours or at run completion (we can implement a scheduled revoke)
- Monitoring hooks: token-level latency metrics, GPU memory, and XPU eviction alerts to a dedicated Slack channel

If those are provided, I can propose EXC parameters and a tentative allocation id.

Marcus

Thanks everyone — reviewed the attachments and Marcus's asks. Approve a temporary carve-out under the following conditions:

- Allocation: reserve 6 H100-80GB equivalents in pool "dedicated-rl-pilot-us-west" (allocation id ALLOC-2026-447)
- Duration: 48 hours by default; ops can extend to 72 hours if no system-level events occur and Orbit confirms (extension request must be submitted 12 hours before end).
- Autoscale exception: EXC-2026-57 created to set min replicas = 6 and disable preemptive eviction for that allocation. Exception includes an automated revoke at T+48h unless extended.
- Runbook: Laura to publish a one-page runbook in the internal runbook link (see related_links) with rollback triggers: CPU/GPU saturation >90% for 15m, queue growth >300%, or infra incident declared. If triggered, ops will revoke EXC and start evacuation playbook.
- Monitoring: dedicated Grafana dashboard + pager to infra-oncall for any eviction or thermal events.

Marcus — please post the GPU-hour estimate here so Karthik can finalize procurement. Bethany — please confirm Orbit's commit window so I can schedule the carve.

Evelyn
